The lounge host flagged a thought on bedding supplies after a rushed handover. Incident note on bedding and cabin comfort

The issue started when the companion animal staging area was opened for the flight and the blanket stack did not match the boarding list. A small spill had already dampened part of the bedding shelf, and the spare pack was left in the wrong bin after the handover from the lounge crew. The cabin team then took the pet carrier through the check path and found the lining for Luna needed changing before boarding. The traveler looked worried, and the temperature near the rear seats also felt uneven for a short stretch, so the situation was handled as a service fault and possible comfort risk rather than a simple supply miss.

The lounge host said <<FACT F113>> and then stayed with the desk while the senior coordinator checked the remaining stock. The carrier was moved to a clean area, fresh bedding was issued, and the damp items were sealed for laundry review. A quick sweep was done around the staging shelf, and the crew was reminded to keep animal supplies separate from general lounge linen. The traveler was told to watch for any sign of stress in the pet and to speak up right away if the cabin felt too warm again. Another crew member relayed that <<FACT F117>> and the note was added to the service log without delay.

Follow-up now sits with the shift lead and the cabin team. They will review the handover order, restock the bedding drawer, and check whether the cooling vents near that row need another look before the next departure. The records aide has also flagged the lounge shelf for a cleaner label system so the same mix-up does not land again. No injury was seen during the event, but the response needs to stay firm and careful. The service file remains open until the review is complete.
